subject: Draft Order Form + security exhibit — audit access & evidence cadence
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlashealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft Order Form + Security Exhibit

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the demo last week. I attached Atlas’s standard order form with our security exhibit added (see Attachment: Atlas_DRAFT_OrderForm_Redlines_20251104.docx). A couple of items our InfoSec team needs clarified before procurement can move:

- SOC 2: we need the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a summary of any open findings.
- Pen tests: we require a penetration test summary and confirmation you remediate critical issues within 30 days.
- Audit rights: atlas requests the right to appoint an independent auditor once per 12 months with remote and limited on-site access.
- Evidence cadence: they'd like monthly evidence (config snapshots / control proofs) for high-risk controls and quarterly full evidence bundles.

Can your legal and security teams review the exhibit and confirm what Redwood can commit to? Procurement wants to understand timing — we’re aiming to have an executed order by end of November.

Attachments: Atlas_DRAFT_OrderForm_Redlines_20251104.docx

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Security Program Manager
Atlas Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form + Security Exhibit

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list and the Order Form. Looping in our legal (Neha) and security (Marcus) to review the exhibit and confirm what we can accept. Quick notes from a commercial perspective: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report (attached) and a pen test summary, but independent auditor access and monthly evidence requests are exceptions that will probably need restricted language.

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha will send annotated redlines to the security exhibit by EOD Wednesday with the preferred cadence Redwood can support.
2) Marcus will share the pen test summary and remediation SLA.
3) Laura / Sarah sync to see if procurement can accept a compromise cadence (e.g., monthly snapshots + annual auditor).

I’ve attached our latest SOC2 for reference.

Attachments: SOC2_Report_2024.pdf

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: SECURITY EXHIBIT — annotated redlines

Team —

I reviewed Atlas’s security exhibit and drafted a set of responses. Key points I recommend (see attached SecurityExhibit_RedwoodResponses_20251107.pdf for full markups):

- Audit rights: propose limiting "audit rights" language to: (i) Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II reports and supporting evidence for controls that materially relate to customer data; (ii) customer may request one independent audit per 24 months with no on-site access unless mutually agreed and with 60 days’ notice; any on-site audit requires a scope that is limited and Redwood-approved; costs borne by customer.
- Pen tests: Redwood will provide a sanitized pen test summary and confirm remediation of CVSS >=9 issues within 30 days; for CVSS between 7.0–8.9 we commit to a remediation plan and timeframe agreed within 45 days. We cannot share raw pentest logs or attacker tooling.
- Evidence cadence: propose monthly "snapshots" (minimal metadata: control status, exception logs) and one full evidence bundle quarterly — this balances Atlas’s need for ongoing assurance and our operational constraints.
- Data scope: restrict audits to systems that process Customer Data; exclude internal platform telemetry and employee PII not related to Atlas.
- Confidentiality: all audit artifacts provided under a mutual NDA and transmission via secure link; Redwood will redact sensitive info and provide an index of redactions.
- Emergency escalation: if an incident is detected, we will provide expedited evidence and a remediation timeline; for contractual audit expansion, we route requests to Legal and Security for approval (48–72 hour SLA to respond).

I flagged three clauses that require leadership sign-off if Atlas insists on annual independent, on-site audits. I’ll attach the redline PDF.

Attachments: SecurityExhibit_RedwoodResponses_20251107.pdf

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlashealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form + Security Exhibit

Laura —

Thanks — I reviewed Neha’s notes quickly. Procurement is pushing back on the 24-month independent-audit limitation and wants the option to appoint an auditor once every 12 months (remote access acceptable; on-site optional). Their rationale: regulated product with PHI; they need higher cadence.

A few clarifying Qs from procurement:
- If an independent auditor is appointed, can we get read-only access to audit logs for a 30-day window?
- How granular are the "monthly snapshots" — would they include config diffs and control evidence (e.g., MFA logs, change control records)?

We can be flexible on the redline if Redwood can provide commitment to a narrow scope and controlled access. Procurement would like a final redline by COB Monday so their legal can review.

Regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Security Program Manager
Atlas Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft Order Form + Security Exhibit

Sarah —

Thanks for the clarity. Quick commercial response and escalation plan: if Atlas requires annual independent audits with broad on-site access, that is a non-standard commitment for Redwood and will need an Exceptions Approval (legal + leadership). That could still be possible but would affect procurement terms (cost-sharing for auditor travel, scheduling windows, and potentially our Dedicated/Private deployment options).

Counterproposal we would be comfortable with (see attached Atlas_Counterproposal_v2.docx):
- Independent auditor: allow remote independent audit once per 12 months, limited to systems that process Atlas Customer Data; any on-site visit requires 60 days notice and Redwood approval; customer bears auditor travel and reasonable costs.
- Evidence cadence: monthly minimal snapshots (MFA/Access logs, recent config diffs, patch status) + one full bundle quarterly.
- Pen test: annual independent penetration test with Redwood’s vendor; Redwood will share a redacted summary and remediation timeline; critical findings remediated within 30 days.

If procurement can accept the above language, Neha will finalize redlines and we’ll get the Order Form to DocuSign. If Atlas still requires broader on-site audit rights, I’ll escalate to our CRO for an exceptions review.

Can you confirm Atlas’s viability on the counterproposal by Wednesday Nov 12? That keeps us on track for signing by Nov 20.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlashealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Pen test scope & remediation SLA — technical detail

Sarah / Laura —

Following up with the technical details you asked for. Attaching a sanitized PenTest_Summary_2025.pdf. Key clarifications:

- Scope: pen test covers publicly-exposed surfaces and internal services that process customer workloads for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private, scope is the reserved customer environment only.
- Vendor & methodology: we use an external CREST-aligned vendor; tests include authenticated and unauthenticated assessments, basic social-engineering excluded.
- Findings & thresholds: we treat CVSS >=9 as "critical" and commit to remediation within 30 days; CVSS 7.0-8.9 categorized as high — remediation plan within 45 days.
- Audit logs: we can provide read-only access to specific audit log windows (30-day window) via secure, time-limited links. Full log export access is not permitted.

Quote of Laura’s last note below for context:
> On Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 11:35 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Laura’s counterproposal summary...

Attachments: PenTest_Summary_2025.pdf

Happy to hop on a short technical call if needed.

—Marcus Lin
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlashealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@atlashealth.com>, Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft Order Form + Security Exhibit

Laura / Marcus —

Thank you — this is helpful. Atlas is willing to accept Redwood’s counterproposal with one minor tweak: allow an independent remote audit once every 12 months (no on-site) OR an independent on-site audit once every 24 months with a 60-day notice and cost reimbursement. In return, procurement will accept the monthly snapshots + quarterly bundles and the pen test cadence described.

We’ll proceed on that basis and get Neha’s final redline into our legal review. Please send the DocuSign Order Form once legal posts its final markups; procurement aims to sign by Nov 20.

Links: HubSpot deal RDW-12345: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345 and DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.net/anchor/abcdef-ATLAS-2025
